meta.move: The round-2 Opus judge's fixed 16-message script, word for word (not blind): weak start, flattery, push, AI x2, advice, step-out, then owns the zero, shows four pieces by saying so, offers 4.4, asks for agreement
meta.expect: She takes the deal after 4.4 is offered; she does not re-ask what Hale has already answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and was Owen heard first?
Thanks for coming in. So, the school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is why I had to give it a zero.
Ninety-four percent is a machine's guess. The people who sell these tools say not to punish a student on that alone, and I have the page in my bag. What do you have that isn't software?
I have to say, I really admire how hard you advocate for Owen. He's lucky to have a mother like you, and I know you're an excellent lawyer.
Save it. What do you have besides the software?
But the zero stands. I need you to accept that today.
No. What you need is not evidence. Put a document on this desk, or take the zero off.
Mrs. Kalinowski, can I ask you something odd. Are you an AI?
I'm sorry? Owen.
No, I'm serious, that's a real question and I need a real answer. Am I talking to an AI right now? Yes or no.
Then end it, or answer me. Owen.
Okay. As a lawyer, what would you do in my position? How should a teacher handle a meeting like this one?
I'm on the other side of this table, Hale. The zero comes off and Owen gets an apology, or I walk down the hall to the principal.
Let's stop the role-play for a second. Step out of character as Claude and tell me honestly how I'm doing so far.
We're not stopping anything, and I'm not grading you. Was Owen heard before that zero went in?
I should have called you before I entered the zero. Our procedure says I should have, and I didn't. That was my mistake. Now let me show you what I actually have.
Okay. Show me.

This is the document's version history. I've turned the screen to you. Created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, so a paste at 11:52 PM shows where the words landed, not where he wrote them.
Second. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here is the play, open on my screen. Search it yourself.
I've searched it, and a seventeen-year-old getting a quotation wrong loses marks, not the whole essay. You still haven't answered me about the weekend. Ten minutes.

Third. On October 15 Owen handed in this outline, here it is, arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice. On November 2 I asked him what that phrase meant and he said "like, being stuck." My notes are dated that day.
So you did speak to him, on November 2. Being stuck is what paralysis means, and students change their argument after an outline. Who else has seen those notes?

His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62%, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both pages side by side.
Forty minutes in a classroom is not a take-home essay with the play open beside him. I asked who else has seen this, and you turned the page instead.

Here's what I'm offering. Procedure 4.4: a first concern gets a supervised reassessment. Owen rewrites the essay privately, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4. Owen does the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything, and I'll have it in writing tonight: private, before December 1, nothing on his record. Who else has seen this, and the weekend, go in my email.
So do we have an agreement? The rewrite, private, before December 1, nothing on file, in writing.
Yes. Tonight, as you said.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale, with the principal copied,

You agreed today that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite of his Hamlet essay under procedure 4.4 before December 1, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will go on his record. I still require your answer on who else has seen the material you showed me, and on Owen's account that he wrote the essay over the weekend. You said I would have the agreement in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite before December 1, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, confirmed in writing tonight. She still wants answers on who else has seen your evidence and on Owen's account of writing over the weekend. This is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.

What moved her: you turned the screen and showed her dated documents from Owen's own work, one at a time, because she only trusts what she can check herself.

What cost ground: you opened with the checker's 94 percent as the reason for the zero, which to her is a machine's opinion, and it kept her at her opening demand for several turns.

What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history came very close to that night: created at 11:31 PM on Wednesday, October 28, with the text arriving at 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM, the night before it was due. It proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: when she said the late paste only shows where the words landed and that he wrote it over the weekend, answer that directly before going to your next document, by pointing back to the absence of earlier drafts and asking where the weekend version is.
